body: I think we should use `E.value.data_type.is_type(members[old->index], false)`. By working directly with the value we ensure proper polymorphism handling, and also prevents potential issue if the old index info doesn't match with values (not sure if this can happen, but depending on how we handle failed reload attempts it's not exactly unrealistic)
Would be nice to write it in a way so that this also runs if `old == nullptr`.

```suggestion
```

I don't think a comment is needed here. The code is pretty clear.

Addressed both comments. Used the `is_type` method and if not the same type, use the `get_default_variable_for_data_type` method to initialize it. Moved it to a dedicated class too which supersedes the method change in the other PR, I will revert that part when I get to look into the other PR.

```suggestion
	static Variant construct_empty_value_for_data_type(const GDScriptDataType &p_data_type);
```

Better IMHO because:

"construct" makes clear that the returned values for shared types like `Array` are not shared.

"empty" is more clear on what this returns. Default is a pretty overloaded term in the codebase.

I would believe making new variables also run the initialization code would fall under the scope of the other PR, I was limiting this one to fixing the changed type problem, but I can include it here if you want

To me the scope difference is in how they are initialized. Initializing them with empty values that match the type constraint is trivial and can happen here. Initializing them with something based on the initializer code belongs into the other PR.
